reason: The cited evidence shows that local compositional fluctuations and ordering affect dislocation behavior and strength (E1, E2, E9), but none of the passages directly demonstrate that SRO variations among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni subsets govern the specific strength-ductility trade-off proposed. The link between SRO and the predicted inverse strength-ductility relationship is not empirically established in the cited works.
premises: Compositional modifications in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni subsets alter local chemical short-range order (SRO).
Increased SRO enhances dislocation pinning, raising yield strength and reducing ductility.
Reduced SRO facilitates dislocation motion, lowering strength but increasing uniform elongation.
SRO can be quantified by APT, neutron diffuse scattering, and simulations.
SRO variations are the primary driver of mechanical property differences among these alloys.
